newsitem.title: USA: Fran weakens inland after bashing the Carolinas.
newsitem.headline: Fran weakens inland after bashing the Carolinas.

text.p: Hurricane warnings were discontinued for North Carolina Friday morning as Fran, downgraded to a tropical storm, moved inland and weakened, with heavy rains posing a serious risk of flooding, National Hurricane Center said.
At 0800 EDT/1200 GMT, Fran's center was near latitude 36.8 north and longitude 79.1 west, or about 20 miles (32 km) north-northeast of Danville, Va., and moving north-northwest near 17 mph (27 kmh).
"This general motion is expected to continue with the center moving across Virginia and West Virginia on Friday.

Maximum sustained winds had weakened to 55 mph (88 kmh), weakening expected to continue as Fran moved farther inland. Tropical storm force winds extended outward up to 290 miles (465 km) from Fran's center, mainly over water.

Forecasters said rainfall totals of 6 to 8 inches (15-20 cm) were possible over parts of North Carolina, Virginia, Maryland, West Virginia and Pennsylvania, along the path of the storm, with the potential for inland flooding.
Isolated tornadoes also remain possible over Virginia and North Carolina.
A tropical storm warning remained in effect from the North Carolina-Virginia border to Chincoteague, Va., including the Greater Hampton Roads area and the Lower Chesapeake Bay.
